chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila, Al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zaid al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Rafath, Fusooq, and Al-Jidal.

He said: As for Rafath, it is sexual intercourse; and as for Fusooq, it is lying. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance'? And Al-Jidal is a man saying: 'No, by Allah' and 'Yes, by Allah', and the verbal insult of one man to another.
ai.seo_question: What are the definitions of Rafath, Fusooq, and Jidal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides precise exegetical definitions for the terms in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:6), linking 'Rafath' to sexual intercourse, 'Fusooq' to lying, and 'Al-Jidal' to contentious argumentation. This interpretation clarifies the specific behaviors that characterize a 'Fasiq' in the context of receiving news, emphasizing that verbal insolence and deceit are key markers of moral deviation. The hadith serves as a practical guide for distinguishing between mere disagreement and the disruptive 'Jidal' warned against in the Quran.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Abu Jamela, Mufaddal bin Saleh, from Zaid al-Shahham, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about approach (to sex), impiety and arguing.

He said: As for approach (to sex), it is sexual intercourse, and as for impiety, it is lying. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «O you who have believed, if an impious comes to you with news, then investigate from having accused a people out of ignorance.» [49:6] Arguing is the saying of a man: «No, by Allah» and «Sure, by Allah», and the verbal insult of a man to another man.
